title: A Visitor From Another Star Is Made of Dusty Ice
summary:
A comet from another star system is giving scientists a rare look at how planets might form around other stars.

The comet, called 3I/ATLAS, was found entering our solar system in the summer of 2025. The James Webb Space Telescope quickly started following it.

Scientists know 3I/ATLAS was not born in our solar system, but nobody knows which star it formed around. It was likely made in a planet-forming disk of gas and dust around a young star, possibly 10 to 12 billion years ago, more than twice the age of our solar system. Then it was thrown out of its home system and left to wander in space.

When the telescope looked at 3I/ATLAS, scientists found a puzzle: the shorter water-ice lines were missing, while the three-micron line stayed strong.

Modeling suggested 3I/ATLAS was made of tiny grains of dirty water-ice, rich in dust, unlike our solar system's much cleaner, almost pure water-ice grains. "Those grains hold clues to the conditions where the comet was born," said research lead author Silvia Protopapa.
why_it_matters: A comet from another star is like a letter from a faraway place, telling us how planets might form around other stars.
